abstract.p: This study reports the details of the Entity-Aware Machine Translation model proposed by the YNU-HPCC team to participate in the SemEval 2025, Task 2. The task focuses on Entity-Aware Machine Translation (EA-MT) to enhance the translation of sentences containing challenging named entities. We investigated traditional machine translation (MT) and large language model (LLM)-based approaches, evaluating their performance using metrics such as M-ETA, and COMET. We integrated a BERTbased Named Entity Recognition (NER) module for the traditional MT system. This approach is simple and intuitive, providing fast performance for common NE categories while achieving accuracy at the standard level. In the LLM-based system, we leveraged multiple LLMs and designed tailored prompts supplemented with a few examples, to guide the model in recognizing named entities. The system effectively translated these entities with high precision by incorporating contextual information from the rest of the sentence. A comparative evaluation of both methods aims to provide insights for future research. More details can be found here. 1
